etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin ratiō. Doublet of ration and reason.

definitions.definition: A number representing a comparison between two named things.
(arithmetic) The relative magnitudes of two quantities (usually expressed as a quotient).
(Internet) The number of comments to a post or other expression on social media relative to the number of likes; a high ratio suggests disagreement with the contents of the original post.
(transitive, Internet slang) To respond to a post or message on social media in a greater number than the number of likes the post receives, especially to condemn or mock the original poster.

quote.citation: 2019, Henry Chisholm, "'Who Cares? It's women's hoops'", Montana Kaimin (The University of Montana), 30 January 2019 - 5 February 2019, page 29:
quote.text: It used to be fun to watch tweets like that get ratioed back into their ugly corner of the internet.

quote.citation: 2021 January 27, Leigh Tauss, “Ghost Roast”, in INDY Week, page 4:
quote.text: And, just FYI, here's how brutally the public ratioed that tweet.

quote.citation: 2021, @suburbanpoet, "Ratio or be Ratioed: Reluctant notes on Twitter", Honi Soit (University of Sydney), Week 4, Semester 2 (2021), page 16:
quote.text: It is essential that you ratio anyone who comes for your honour.

definitions.definition: (neologism, Twitter) Indicates disagreement with a post the user disagrees with or dislikes.

quote.citation: 2021, Lil Nas X, THE MONTERO SHOW‎[1]:
quote.text: "Ratio. YoungBoy is better." "What?" "Make better music. You fell off."
